rows.title: Policy
rows.figure: Fed Oct 28 held 3.75–4.00% (10–2, Cook + Hammack for +25bp), Dec hike ~86%; BoC hiked to 2.50%, Dec ~45%; RBNZ held 2.75% (4–3); RBA Nov 3 hike ~79–85%; ECB Oct 29 hold ~95%; BoJ Oct 30 hold ~98%; BoE Nov 5 hike ~94%
rows.read: The Fed held but two officials wanted to hike now, and Canada raised rates, so the global push toward higher rates continues. Fed chair Kevin Warsh refused to commit to December, which took some shine off the dollar. Europe and Japan decide next, and both are expected to wait until December.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Fed statement: activity 'strong' (from 'solid'); US Sep goods deficit −$134.9B (fc −$130.2B); OBR UK 2027 growth 1.0% (from 1.6%); German GfK −30.8; US Q3 GDP Thu fc 3.0% annualised
rows.read: The Fed upgraded its view of the US economy to strong, while Britain's budget watchdog cut its growth forecast and German shoppers stayed gloomy. That gap keeps favouring the dollar. US third-quarter growth figures on Thursday are the next check.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Fed: inflation 'remains elevated'; BoC 2027 inflation forecast 3.1% (from 2.0%); Australia Q3 trimmed CPI +1.0% q/q (RBA fc 0.8%); Tokyo CPI tonight 6:30 PM CT; US core PCE Thu fc +0.3% m/m
rows.read: Energy keeps pushing prices up: the Fed called inflation elevated, Canada raised its inflation forecasts and Australia's ran hotter than its central bank expected. That keeps most banks leaning toward hikes, which supports currencies whose banks act. The US inflation measure the Fed watches most comes on Thursday.

rows.title: Risk
rows.figure: US stocks ~+0.2% after the Fed; USD/JPY ~157.8; USD/CHF ~0.830; Israel count ~93%: no bloc near 61 seats; WSJ: US warned Gulf of possible post-midterm Iran campaign
rows.read: Markets stayed calm through the Fed, so the yen and franc drew little demand as safe places for money. The risks are building in the background: a report says the US may strike Iran after the midterms, and Israel's election left no clear winner. A turn in either would test that calm.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$115.7 (+$1.78, late morning); WTI >$103 (one-week high); EIA crude −1.9M bbl (fc ~flat), gasoline +3.9M; OPEC+ meets Sunday
rows.read: Oil rose again on falling US stocks and talk of US strikes on Iran after the midterms. That helps exporters like Canada and Australia and costs importers like Japan and the euro area. Until the talks with Iran produce terms, the war premium stays in the price.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 20: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against NZD (sharply added) and EUR (added), for GBP (real money strongly against), for AUD (real money strongly against), leaning against JPY, strongly for gold
rows.read: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, but Canada's rate hike today was too cautious to force them to buy loonies back. Their bets against the kiwi paid off after New Zealand's surprise hold. In the pound and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: UK Budget: borrowing 4.2% of GDP this year to 1.8% by 2030–31; headroom £15bn (from £24bn); 10-year gilt yield −2bp; French revenue vote Nov 3; France–Germany 10-year gap ~162–177bp
rows.read: Chancellor John Healey's first UK Budget passed calmly, with borrowing set to fall, so UK bonds and the pound took it in stride. France's budget fight is still unresolved and keeps a weight on the euro.
